report:
Reviewed meta.reviews.complete_test_set independently using its complete four-line claim, the whole associated review.rs implementation file, the complete associated test, and recorded fixture/specification/eligibility context. Requirements: one review is scoped to one anchor and its complete associated test set; every eligible associated test is captured in deterministic order; tests may divide the claim rather than each independently proving it.

Implementation: inventory iterates spec.anchors and builds one ReviewInput per anchor, beginning with that anchor's Claim fragment. It traverses every entry in rust.tests.get(name), captures the complete function source and identifying metadata, sorts and deduplicates ReviewTest metadata, and emits function fragments from a BTreeMap keyed by file/package/target/Rust path. Thus separate functions are retained, repeated identical associations do not invent tests, and both metadata and fragment ordering are deterministic. Conflicting spans for one selector identity are rejected instead of silently losing a function. The one input contains the claim and all these tests; neither inventory nor acceptance demands each test independently establish the claim. start selects one anchor input, and input_errors compares the entire test vector and initial fragments, so adding or removing a test requires a fresh collective assessment. The captured correspondence context confirms that the upstream associated-test set accepts module-level built-in test functions in enabled harnesses and rejects ignored tests; this is supporting inventory context, while the complete-set aggregation itself is implemented in the associated review.rs file.

All associated evidence is ordinary: one implementation entry at the inventory sorting/fragment emission region and one annotated test, added_or_removed_associations_invalidate_unchanged_saved_fragments. No TODO/N/A rationale or deferred requirement exists. The test starts with a one-test fixture, adds a distinct second annotated function, asserts validation fails, asserts the fresh input contains two tests, and compares repeated starts for deterministic test metadata. It explicitly verifies that the original function's metadata remains in the set. After recording that two-test input it removes the second function and asserts validation fails again. Its final implementation-association addition assertion also verifies collective association freshness, beyond this anchor's test-set requirement. The visible body therefore detects dropping the added function, losing the original function, changing output ordering between starts, and failure to invalidate after test-set changes. Fixture helpers only construct files and invoke actual start/record/check operations; meaningful assertions are visible in the annotated test body. Allowing tests to divide a claim is a permissive review policy, reflected by one aggregate input and absence of per-test sufficiency enforcement, not a requirement that each fixture test implement all prose.

Current refresh: the complete claim, whole implementation file, prompt and association metadata match my previous independent inspection. I inspected the complete fresh test body. It now adds a review_diagnostics association and replaces each negative is_valid assertion with ensure_valid().unwrap_err() plus explicit assertions naming demo.rule, the changed test/implementation association category, and the review skill. These strengthen the previous negative checks: the saved collective review must reject additions and removals for the relevant association reason. The two-test count, deterministic repeated-start equality, preserved original test identity, and final two-implementation count remain unchanged. Captured ensure_valid confirms it returns an error on invalid CheckReport and joins diagnostic messages; the test assertions are meaningful, not an opaque success wrapper. Recaptured fixture setup through line 106 (avoiding unnecessary following test bodies), the review specification and eligibility helper ranges. No TODO/N/A, omitted claim aspect or unresolved concern was found.

Execution: this refresh personally ran review start/read commands and source comparisons; no source edits or redundant test runs were performed. My earlier focused test run passed before the latest diagnostic-assertion changes and is not claimed as execution of this revision. The coordinator reports 331 sage-meta functional tests, 46 sage-stash tests and workspace build passed against current sources; these are reported coordinator results, not commands I personally executed. This complete assessment is based on current captured source and the explicit assertions described above.
